|: A2 c cdc cdc | A2 c cdc f2 a | A2 c cdc cdc | d2 d def gec :|
|: A2 c A2 c AGF | A2 c A2 c BAG | A2 c A2 c AGF | d2 d def gec :|
|: a3 g3 f3 | d2 d def gec | a3 g3 f3 | d2 d c2 B AGF :|

The ‘manuscript book’ the above transcription was taken from was compiled by a James Hook, Junior, containing over 200 melodies of various types, and was given to Thomas Hardy’s father around 1820. I believe that said manuscript is now in The Dorset County Museum collection…

Blewitt’s Jig

Included in the collection “Hamilton’s Universal Tune Book” (Glasgow, 1844) under the title “Blewitt’s Jig”. The notes say, “This favourite jig, to which Mr Hudson’s song of ”Barny Brallaghan’s Courtship“ is sung, is printed by the kind permission of the composer, Mr I Blewitt.”

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on August 12th, 2013.

Barney Brannigan

X:5 from a 1933 Leo Rowsome 78. Leo first played the Drops of Brandy, necessarily having to keep a lightning pace at it to match the 2nd tune. Interestingly enough I have a home recording of Leo and Larry Redican where they play this same medley in reverse, with Larry playing the usual setting of BB, resulting in a bit of a mismatch, and giving up to let Leo solo on the Ds of B. Obviously he considered these tunes a pair. I’ve always much favored his setting here, it makes for a great piping jig.

↳ Posted by Lucy Rietmann on November 25th, 2013.

Re: Barney Brannigan

Cameron’s Selection of Violin Music (Glasgow 1859) calls it Blewitt’s Jig and gives the composer as J Blewitt. There is a Wikipedia entry for Jonathan Blewitt (19 July 1782 – 4 September 1853) which says he was a London born composer of light music who worked in Ireland from 1811 to 1820 and after that successfully composed music for the London theatres but died in poverty.
